before.title: Mounjaro cost in the UK: compare the whole quote
before.author: SHIFT Team
before.summary: Compare a dated Mounjaro quote fairly, distinguish list prices from your bill, and check continuing costs, safe supply and clinical responsibilities.
before.body:
# Mounjaro cost in the UK: compare the whole quote

A price for the first pen is not necessarily the price of continuing treatment. Compare the actual written offer, the service providing it and what happens if the dose, supply or your circumstances change.

For the wider picture, read our [Mounjaro UK information](/mounjaro). To compare approaches, use the [weight-loss treatment comparison centre](/compare-weight-loss-treatments).

## List price and your bill are different things

A list price in a NICE appraisal is part of a particular assessment of NHS use. It is not a retail price cap, a private pharmacy quote or evidence that the NHS will pay for an individual person's treatment. Confidential NHS arrangements and private services may have different costs.

This article does not provide a live price league table. Private quotes change, and an old comparison can become misleading. Ask the provider for a dated quote for the exact medicine, formulation, prescribed dose and length of supply.

## Compare like with like

- Does the quote cover four weeks or a calendar month?
- Are consultation, prescription, needles, delivery and any membership charges included?
- What is the quoted cost at later doses if your prescriber considers a change appropriate?
- Is the advertised amount an introductory offer? What happens when it ends?
- What are the cancellation, refund and failed-delivery terms?
- Who assesses you, who prescribes and which registered pharmacy dispenses?
- How do you obtain clinical advice between appointments, and what is included?

Write the answers alongside each provider's quote. A cheaper headline with extra recurring fees may not be a cheaper continuing service. Do not assume a term such as support means clinical monitoring or a particular response time.

## Do not invent a fixed treatment course

Mounjaro is not automatically a twelve- or eighteen-month course. Suitability, dose, review and continuation depend on individual clinical assessment. A spreadsheet can show what a stated quote would cost over a chosen period, but cannot establish how long you should take the medicine.

If affordability is changing, tell the prescribing service early. Ask about a safe plan and any suitable alternatives. Do not stretch doses, extract medicine from a pen or switch products to make a budget work without clinical advice.

## NHS eligibility is a separate question

NICE's recommendation and the local commissioning pathway are not the same as a promise of immediate access. Ask your GP or relevant service which current pathway applies where you live and what support accompanies it. UK arrangements differ; an England appraisal is not a universal rule for every NHS service.

## Keep a record before paying

Save the quote, the terms, the provider and pharmacy details, the order confirmation and the route for clinical questions. If a provider stops replying, use [Clinic Gone Quiet](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/clinic-gone-quiet) to organise the next steps. Urgent symptoms need the appropriate healthcare service, not a billing dispute or a company inbox.

## What My Timber can help with

My Timber can organise practical food, movement and everyday routines during or after treatment. It does not set your medicine dose, approve a switch or supply a clinical review. SHIFT medicine ordering remains closed while the regulated partner is not commissioned. Information on this page is not an offer to prescribe or dispense.

## Sources and editorial note

- [NICE TA1026: tirzepatide for managing overweight and obesity](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ta1026).
- [Mounjaro: current UK product information](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/15484/smpc).
- [MHRA: information about GLP-1 medicines](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/glp-1-medicines-for-weight-loss-and-diabetes-what-you-need-to-know/glp-1-medicines-for-weight-loss-and-diabetes-what-you-need-to-know).

Editorial correction: 2 October 2026. Stale price ranges, list-price comparisons presented as retail limits and a fixed treatment-duration assumption have been removed. No medicine catalogue, stock or service price has been changed. General information; independent clinical review is not claimed.

before.title: Missed a Wegovy injection: the UK leaflet’s rules
before.author: SHIFT Team
before.summary: The UK weekly-injection leaflet’s five-day boundary, usual scheduled day, longer treatment gaps and when to contact your pharmacist or prescriber.
before.body:
# Missed a Wegovy injection: the UK leaflet’s rules

You remembered the shopping, the school run and that work thing you were meant to finish yesterday. The injection slipped through. Now the calendar is open and every website seems to have a different answer.

Start with the exact medicine in your hand. This page is about **UK Wegovy weekly injections**, not Wegovy tablets, Ozempic or Mounjaro. Their instructions are not interchangeable. If your own leaflet or prescriber has given you different instructions, ask your pharmacist or prescriber to resolve that difference.

**Checked against UK product information on 2 October 2026. This is general information, not an individual restart or prescribing decision.**

## The single missed-dose rule

The UK [Wegovy patient leaflet](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/files/pil.13800.pdf) distinguishes two situations:

- **Five days or less have passed since the injection was due:** use the missed dose as soon as you remember, then take the next dose on your usual scheduled day.
- **More than five days have passed:** skip the missed injection and take the next dose on your usual scheduled day.
- **Do not double the dose** to make up for a missed one.

The boundary matters: the leaflet includes day five in the first case. An article saying “five days or more means skip” changes that instruction.

Count from when the injection was due, not from when you noticed you had forgotten it. If you cannot work out the dates, do not fill the gap with a best guess. Your dispensing pharmacist or prescriber can help you check what the instructions mean for your situation.

## A missed dose does not automatically create a new weekly day

The missed-dose instructions say to return to the **usual scheduled day**. They do not tell everyone to put the next injection seven days after the late one.

Deliberately changing your regular injection day is a separate instruction in the [UK Summary of Product Characteristics](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/13800/smpc). It specifies a gap of more than 72 hours between doses when changing the day. That is not a reason to invent a different catch-up schedule.

If the missed-dose instructions and a planned day change leave you uncertain, check with your pharmacist or prescriber before acting. This page cannot choose a dosing date for you.

## More than one dose missed, or a longer break

A longer interruption needs a conversation with the service responsible for your prescription. The product information says a lower starting dose may need to be considered when restarting after more doses have been missed. It does not provide one restart strength that is right for everybody.

Do not choose a lower or higher strength from an online table, use somebody else's pen, or try to make up all the missing injections. Your prescriber needs to know the gap, what you were taking and how you were tolerating it.

You can make that conversation easier without needing to become a medication expert. Write down:

1. The exact medicine, pen strength and dispensing pharmacy.
2. The date of your last injection, if known.
3. The date the next injection was due and which doses you missed.
4. Any symptoms you have now or had before the gap.
5. Other medicines and relevant changes in your health.

If a date is approximate, say so. Accurate uncertainty is more useful than a confident invented date.

## Symptoms change the priority

A calendar problem and a concerning symptom are different jobs. Severe, persistent stomach pain, especially if it spreads to your back or comes with sickness, needs urgent medical attention. The [MHRA's pancreatitis warning](https://www.gov.uk/drug-safety-update/glp-1-receptor-agonists-and-dual-glp-1-slash-gip-receptor-agonists-strengthened-warnings-on-acute-pancreatitis-including-necrotising-and-fatal-cases) applies to these medicines.

Repeated vomiting, inability to keep fluids down or signs of serious dehydration also need medical advice. Use appropriate urgent NHS care when needed; do not wait for a routine company inbox.

Tell the clinician which medicine you use, including privately prescribed treatment. If pancreatitis is confirmed, the MHRA advises that treatment must not be restarted. A clinician should assess the symptoms and treatment; a website cannot diagnose what is happening.

## Make the next week less dependent on memory

Once the medicine question is settled, choose a reminder system you will actually notice. A weekly phone reminder and a note of the date you really took the injection are more useful than three different apps with three different dates.

Keep the record simple:

| Record | What to write |
| --- | --- |
| Regular day | The day agreed for your normal schedule |
| Actual injection | Date and medicine/strength used |
| Missed or delayed | What happened, without filling in an injection you did not take |
| Advice received | Who advised you, when, and the instructions they gave |

When travelling or changing routines, take the leaflet and pharmacy contact details with you. Discuss uncertainties rather than borrowing a rule for a different product or country.

You do not need a perfect streak. You need a record that tells the truth when you look back at it.

## What SHIFT can help with

My Timber provides everyday food, movement, check-ins and progress support. It does not decide whether you should inject, choose a restart dose or provide a commissioned clinician-led missed-dose service.

For the medicine question, contact your dispensing pharmacy or prescriber. If your clinic has stopped replying, the [clinic-gone-quiet guide](/clinic-gone-quiet) can help you organise records and find the appropriate next route. Urgent symptoms still need urgent care.

For the ordinary part of the week, you can keep using [free My Timber](/member/dashboard). A missed injection does not need to turn into abandoning every useful meal, walk or routine. Pick one manageable thing for today, then return to see whether it helped.

## Sources and correction note

- [UK Wegovy patient leaflet](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/files/pil.13800.pdf): patient instructions for a forgotten dose.
- [UK Wegovy SmPC](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/13800/smpc): missed doses, re-initiation and changing the weekly day.
- [MHRA safety update, 29 January 2026](https://www.gov.uk/drug-safety-update/glp-1-receptor-agonists-and-dual-glp-1-slash-gip-receptor-agonists-strengthened-warnings-on-acute-pancreatitis-including-necrotising-and-fatal-cases): urgent pancreatitis symptoms.

Editorial correction, 2 October 2026: this replaces the earlier inconsistent five-day boundary, automatic schedule-reset advice and uncommissioned SHIFT clinical-service claims. It contains no invented quotation from Matt and makes no claim of independent clinical review.

before.title: Wegovy side effects: how long do they last?
before.author: SHIFT Team
before.summary: Wegovy injection side effects can ease over time, but duration varies. Know common symptoms, practical support and when to get urgent medical help.
before.body:
**Wegovy injection side effects often ease over time, but there is no reliable day or week when they must stop.** Digestive symptoms occur most often while the dose is being increased. Some people have few symptoms; others need help from their prescribing clinician. Persistent, worsening or severe symptoms should be assessed rather than measured against an online timetable.

This guide covers **Wegovy injections**. Use the leaflet supplied with your exact product. Tablets and other semaglutide brands have their own instructions.

## Warning signs: get help first

**Severe abdominal pain that persists, especially if it spreads to your back:** stop using Wegovy and seek urgent medical help immediately, as instructed in the patient leaflet. Pain with or without nausea or vomiting can indicate pancreatitis. Do not wait for your next routine review. The [MHRA pancreatitis warning](https://www.gov.uk/drug-safety-update/glp-1-receptor-agonists-and-dual-glp-1-slash-gip-receptor-agonists-strengthened-warnings-on-acute-pancreatitis-including-necrotising-and-fatal-cases) explains why this needs prompt assessment.

**Sudden loss of vision or rapidly worsening eyesight:** urgently contact a doctor. The [Wegovy injection leaflet](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/13801/pil) warns about a very rare eye condition called NAION. Changes in vision can also have other causes.

**Sudden swelling of your mouth, tongue or throat, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or collapse:** call **999**. These can be signs of [anaphylaxis](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/anaphylaxis/), a life-threatening allergic reaction.

**Repeated vomiting and inability to keep fluids down:** seek urgent advice now. Dark urine, less urine than usual, or dizziness on standing that does not settle can indicate serious dehydration. If dehydration comes with confusion, difficulty waking, cold skin or breathing problems, call **999**. See [NHS dehydration advice](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/dehydration/).

**Sudden severe stomach pain, blood in vomit or vomit resembling coffee grounds:** call **999 or go to A&E**, following [NHS vomiting guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/diarrhoea-and-vomiting/).

## How long do Wegovy side effects last?

The [UK prescribing information](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/13801/smpc) reports digestive effects most frequently during dose escalation. In trials, most nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea episodes were mild to moderate and relatively short; constipation often lasted longer. These are group findings, not a forecast for your symptoms.

A dose increase can bring symptoms, but symptoms appearing later still deserve attention. The number of days since your injection cannot tell you whether a problem is safe to ignore.

The useful questions are: **is it improving, can I keep fluids down, and is it interfering with eating, sleep or ordinary activity?** Tell your prescribing service if symptoms are troublesome or persistent. It may need to reassess your treatment.

Do not increase, reduce, restart or switch your medicine yourself. Significant digestive symptoms may lead a prescriber to delay an increase or adjust treatment; that decision belongs with them.

## What are the common side effects?

The current injection leaflet groups these effects by frequency:

| Frequency in the leaflet | Examples |
|---|---|
| Very common: more than 1 in 10 people | Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal pain, headache, weakness or tiredness |
| Common: up to 1 in 10 people | Indigestion, reflux or heartburn, burping, wind, bloating, dizziness, hair loss and injection-site reactions |

This is not the complete list. “Common” does not mean that a severe symptom is harmless. Bowel obstruction is also listed, with frequency unknown: severe constipation alongside pain, bloating or vomiting needs medical assessment.

## What can help with mild symptoms?

These are general NHS self-care measures, not a diagnosis or a substitute for assessing warning signs.

### Feeling sick

[NHS nausea guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/feeling-sick-nausea/) suggests smaller, more frequent meals and regular sips of a cold drink. Eat slowly. Avoid greasy or fried food, strong cooking smells and lying down soon after eating.

For a working day, that could mean taking a smaller lunch and keeping a drink within reach instead of trying to finish a large meal while feeling sick. Choose food you can tolerate; there is no need to force a particular recipe.

If nausea does not improve over a few days or keeps returning, speak to your GP or prescribing clinician.

### Diarrhoea or vomiting

Rest and take small sips of fluid. Eat when you feel able; fatty or spicy food may be harder to manage. Fruit juice and fizzy drinks can worsen diarrhoea. A pharmacist can advise whether an oral rehydration product is suitable.

Do not use the usual duration of a stomach bug as a deadline for medicine-related symptoms. If you cannot keep fluids down, seek urgent help.

### Constipation

For uncomplicated constipation, [NHS advice](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/constipation/) includes regular fluids, gradually increasing dietary fibre, gentle daily activity and allowing time for the toilet. Avoid delaying the urge to go.

If these measures do not help, ask a pharmacist about appropriate treatment. Persistent constipation, blood in your stool or a change in bowel habits needs a GP assessment. Pain and vomiting alongside constipation need prompt assessment.

## What should I tell my prescriber?

Keep a short record you can read out or send directly to the prescribing service:

- Exact medicine, formulation and prescribed dose.
- Date of your last injection and any recent change.
- Symptom, when it started, and whether it is improving.
- Vomiting or diarrhoea episodes, and whether fluids stay down.
- Changes in urine, bowel movements or eyesight.
- Other medicines, supplements and remedies you have taken.
- Effect on eating, sleep, work and usual activity.

For example: “Since Tuesday I have felt sick after meals. I can keep drinks down, but I have eaten less. My last injection was Monday; my dose recently changed.” Add what is true for you. **Do not delay urgent care to finish the record.**

[NHS semaglutide information](https://www.nhs.uk/medicines/semaglutide/) advises speaking to a pharmacist or doctor about effects that bother you or do not go away. Do not drive or use machinery if dizzy or having vision problems.

## Who can help in the UK?

Contact your prescribing service for treatment decisions. If it cannot respond promptly, use your GP, pharmacist or appropriate urgent service:

| Where you live | Urgent advice route |
|---|---|
| England | [NHS 111](https://www.nhs.uk/nhs-services/urgent-and-emergency-care-services/when-to-use-111/) |
| Scotland | [NHS 24: call 111](https://www.nhs24.scot/111/) |
| Wales | [NHS 111 Wales](https://111.wales.nhs.uk/) |
| Northern Ireland | Your GP, or the [GP out-of-hours service](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/gp-out-hours-service) when your practice is closed |

Call **999 for a life-threatening emergency anywhere in the UK**.

For everyday food planning, our [nutrition and meal-planning guide](/guides/nutrition-protein-calories-meal-planning) gives a practical starting point. It does not diagnose or treat side effects.

My Timber can help organise ordinary routines. It does not assess side effects or send a saved symptom record to a clinician. SHIFT medicine ordering remains closed while the regulated partner is not commissioned.

## Sources and editorial note

Published **23 September 2026**. Sources checked and article expanded **5 October 2026** by SHIFT Team. The FlexTouch patient leaflet on emc was updated **22 September 2026**. This is general information; independent clinical review is not claimed. Follow your own product leaflet and individual professional advice.

You can report a suspected medicine side effect through [MHRA Yellow Card](https://yellowcard.mhra.gov.uk/). Reporting helps medicine safety monitoring; it does not provide medical treatment or urgent advice.

## Make a routine review easier

For a non-urgent conversation, pick questions about symptoms and follow-up with the free review checklist. For symptoms needing urgent help, use the warning signs and healthcare routes above; do not wait for a routine review.

[Build your weight-management review checklist](/tools/weight-management-review)

The [UK prescribing information](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/13801/smpc) reports digestive effects most frequently during dose escalation. In trials, most nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea episodes were mild to moderate and relatively short; constipation often lasted longer. These are group findings, not a forecast for your symptoms.

A dose increase can bring symptoms, but symptoms appearing later still deserve attention. The number of days since your injection cannot tell you whether a problem is safe to ignore.

The useful questions are: **is it improving, can I keep fluids down, and is it interfering with eating, sleep or ordinary activity?** Tell your prescribing service if symptoms are troublesome or persistent. It may need to reassess your treatment.

Do not increase, reduce, restart or switch your medicine yourself. Significant digestive symptoms may lead a prescriber to delay an increase or adjust treatment; that decision belongs with them.

## What are the common side effects?

The current injection leaflet groups these effects by frequency:

| Frequency in the leaflet | Examples |
|---|---|
| Very common: more than 1 in 10 people | Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal pain, headache, weakness or tiredness |
| Common: up to 1 in 10 people | Indigestion, reflux or heartburn, burping, wind, bloating, dizziness, hair loss and injection-site reactions |

This is not the complete list. “Common” does not mean that a severe symptom is harmless. Bowel obstruction is also listed, with frequency unknown: severe constipation alongside pain, bloating or vomiting needs medical assessment.

## What can help with mild symptoms?

These are general NHS self-care measures, not a diagnosis or a substitute for assessing warning signs.

### Feeling sick

[NHS nausea guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/feeling-sick-nausea/) suggests smaller, more frequent meals and regular sips of a cold drink. Eat slowly. Avoid greasy or fried food, strong cooking smells and lying down soon after eating.

For a working day, that could mean taking a smaller lunch and keeping a drink within reach instead of trying to finish a large meal while feeling sick. Choose food you can tolerate; there is no need to force a particular recipe.

If nausea does not improve over a few days or keeps returning, speak to your GP or prescribing clinician.

### Diarrhoea or vomiting

Rest and take small sips of fluid. Eat when you feel able; fatty or spicy food may be harder to manage. Fruit juice and fizzy drinks can worsen diarrhoea. A pharmacist can advise whether an oral rehydration product is suitable.

Do not use the usual duration of a stomach bug as a deadline for medicine-related symptoms. If you cannot keep fluids down, seek urgent help.

### Constipation

For uncomplicated constipation, [NHS advice](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/constipation/) includes regular fluids, gradually increasing dietary fibre, gentle daily activity and allowing time for the toilet. Avoid delaying the urge to go.

If these measures do not help, ask a pharmacist about appropriate treatment. Persistent constipation, blood in your stool or a change in bowel habits needs a GP assessment. Pain and vomiting alongside constipation need prompt assessment.

## What should I tell my prescriber?

Keep a short record you can read out or send directly to the prescribing service:

- Exact medicine, formulation and prescribed dose.
- Date of your last injection and any recent change.
- Symptom, when it started, and whether it is improving.
- Vomiting or diarrhoea episodes, and whether fluids stay down.
- Changes in urine, bowel movements or eyesight.
- Other medicines, supplements and remedies you have taken.
- Effect on eating, sleep, work and usual activity.

For example: “Since Tuesday I have felt sick after meals. I can keep drinks down, but I have eaten less. My last injection was Monday; my dose recently changed.” Add what is true for you. **Do not delay urgent care to finish the record.**

[NHS semaglutide information](https://www.nhs.uk/medicines/semaglutide/) advises speaking to a pharmacist or doctor about effects that bother you or do not go away. Do not drive or use machinery if dizzy or having vision problems.

## Who can help in the UK?

Contact your prescribing service for treatment decisions. If it cannot respond promptly, use your GP, pharmacist or appropriate urgent service:

| Where you live | Urgent advice route |
|---|---|
| England | [NHS 111](https://www.nhs.uk/nhs-services/urgent-and-emergency-care-services/when-to-use-111/) |
| Scotland | [NHS 24: call 111](https://www.nhs24.scot/111/) |
| Wales | [NHS 111 Wales](https://111.wales.nhs.uk/) |
| Northern Ireland | Your GP, or the [GP out-of-hours service](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/gp-out-hours-service) when your practice is closed |

Call **999 for a life-threatening emergency anywhere in the UK**.

For everyday food planning, our [nutrition and meal-planning guide](/guides/nutrition-protein-calories-meal-planning) gives a practical starting point. It does not diagnose or treat side effects.

[My Timber](/my-timber) can help organise ordinary routines. It does not assess side effects or send a saved symptom record to a clinician. SHIFT medicine ordering remains closed while the regulated partner is not commissioned.

## Sources and editorial note

Published **23 September 2026**. Sources checked and article expanded **5 October 2026** by SHIFT Team. The FlexTouch patient leaflet on emc was updated **22 September 2026**. This is general information; independent clinical review is not claimed. Follow your own product leaflet and individual professional advice.

You can report a suspected medicine side effect through [MHRA Yellow Card](https://yellowcard.mhra.gov.uk/). Reporting helps medicine safety monitoring; it does not provide medical treatment or urgent advice.

## Make a routine review easier

For a non-urgent conversation, pick questions about symptoms and follow-up with the free review checklist. For symptoms needing urgent help, use the warning signs and healthcare routes above; do not wait for a routine review.

[Build your weight-management review checklist](/tools/weight-management-review)

before.title: Weight-loss medicines and muscle: what to ask about strength and nutrition
before.author: SHIFT Team
before.summary: Understand the limits of body-composition claims and prepare useful questions about nutrition, suitable strength activity and monitoring.
before.body:
# Weight-loss medicines and muscle: what to ask about strength and nutrition

A falling weight does not tell you how much change came from fat, muscle, fluid or other tissue. Research on body composition needs careful interpretation, and one trial average cannot predict the amount of muscle an individual man will lose.

## Lean mass is not the same measurement as muscle

Body-composition studies often report lean mass or fat-free mass. These measures include more than skeletal muscle. They are not a direct measure of strength, function or whether somebody can carry shopping, climb stairs or get up from a chair.

Study populations, methods, medicine doses and follow-up periods differ. A headline that promises to prevent muscle loss, or applies a single kilogram average to UK men generally, goes further than those measurements support. This page makes neither claim.

## Discuss nutrition before choosing a target

If appetite or intake has changed during treatment, tell the prescribing service what you can actually eat. Ask whether you need support from a registered dietitian. A protein calculator is an estimate, not an individual prescription, particularly where kidney disease, other conditions or a restricted diet affect what is suitable.

Prepare a few practical details: the meals you usually manage, foods you avoid, your budget, cooking facilities and any nausea or swallowing difficulty. Do not assume a supplement solves inadequate overall intake. If you are unable to eat or drink adequately, obtain medical advice rather than relying on this article.

## Keep movement appropriate to your starting point

Strength activities can form part of an ordinary activity plan. The NHS provides beginner strength guidance with supported versions of movements. Choose suitable activity and build gradually; existing pain, balance difficulties or medical conditions may require individual advice.

- Ask which movements and amount are appropriate for you.
- Learn the technique from a reputable guide or qualified professional.
- Notice recovery and symptoms as well as repetitions or weight lifted.
- Include activities you want to do in daily life when discussing progress.
- Avoid using a generic programme as proof that a particular exercise is safe for you.

No exercise plan can guarantee preservation of every kilogram of lean tissue. Do not push through concerning symptoms to satisfy a target.

## Questions for your next review

What should we monitor alongside body weight? Is the rate of change appropriate for my circumstances? Does my food intake need assessment? Would a dietitian, physiotherapist or qualified exercise professional help? When should I seek advice rather than wait for the next appointment?

If a home scale reports a muscle percentage, ask how that estimate is obtained and how to interpret it. Do not change a prescribed medicine because one reading moved.

## What My Timber can help with

Grub and Fit can help organise everyday food and movement choices. They do not provide body-composition assessment, clinical monitoring or a promise to prevent treatment-related muscle loss. Your prescriber remains responsible for treatment decisions. SHIFT medicine ordering remains closed while the regulated partner is not commissioned.

## Sources and editorial note

- [NHS: strength exercises](https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/strength-exercises/).
- [NHS: eating a balanced diet, including individual dietary needs](https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/eat-well/how-to-eat-a-balanced-diet/eating-a-balanced-diet/).
- [Wegovy: current UK product information](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/13800/smpc).

Editorial correction: 2 October 2026. The unsupported universal 1.74 kg headline and prevention promise have been removed. General information; independent clinical or trainer review is not claimed.

before.title: Wegovy not working? Preparing for a treatment review
before.author: SHIFT Team
before.summary: What to record and ask if Wegovy results disappoint, without fixed waiting rules, self-directed dose changes or blame.
before.body:
# Wegovy not working? Preparing for a treatment review

![Decorative Wegovy weight stall title card](https://media.babylovegrowth.ai/blog-images/organization-55073/1790385228551_Decorative-Wegovy-weight-stall-title-card.jpeg)

If your weight is not changing as expected on Wegovy, arrange a review rather than assuming you have failed. Response, prescribed treatment, tolerability and other health factors all deserve consideration. There is no blanket instruction to wait 16–20 weeks or to continue through concerning symptoms. This guide helps you prepare useful information for your prescriber; it does not set a dose or switching plan.

***

> **Key points**
>
> - Slow progress has several possible explanations and cannot be diagnosed from a weight chart alone.
> - Review the exact product and prescribed schedule with your care team.
> - Report troublesome symptoms promptly; urgent symptoms need urgent care.
> - Tests should be chosen for your circumstances, not ordered as a universal checklist.
> - Do not increase, restart or switch treatment using an article.

***

## Common reasons Wegovy may not appear to be working

A review should consider both the treatment and your experience without assuming poor effort or incorrect use. Some people respond less than others even when they follow the plan. It helps to bring reliable records and specific questions rather than trying to identify a single cause yourself.

If treatment is still being adjusted, tell the prescriber exactly what you have taken and for how long. A dose-escalation schedule is intended to manage treatment safely; it is not a promise that appetite or weight will change only after a particular step. You can ask for advice before the end of titration.

Food and activity form part of weight-management care, but a plateau alone does not prove excess eating. Discuss appetite, access to food, symptoms and what is practical in your routine. An honest account is more useful than a stricter diet adopted just before the appointment. If intake is already low, further restriction may be inappropriate.

Ask a pharmacist or prescriber to check administration and storage if you are unsure. Bring the exact product name and instructions. Mention missed doses or supply gaps without embarrassment; this helps them advise safely. Do not take extra doses to make up for a perceived lack of effect.

Topics worth reviewing include:

- **Treatment history:** prescribed doses, interruptions and administration questions.
- **Tolerability:** symptoms, low intake or difficulty drinking.
- **Weight trend:** the length of the apparent plateau and how readings were taken.
- **Other health factors:** new symptoms, diagnoses or medicine changes.
- **Expectations:** whether the goal and review schedule remain appropriate.

Plateaus in particular can feel like failure when they're often just the body adjusting. It's worth reading about how to [check before panicking about a plateau](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/articles/weight-loss-plateau-men) rather than assuming the treatment has stopped working altogether.

**Pro Tip:** *Keep a simple weekly log of your dose, injection day, and roughly what you've eaten. It takes two minutes and gives your clinician something concrete to work from at your next review.*

## How Wegovy dosing and timing affect results

Wegovy's dosing schedule is deliberately slow, and that's often the first thing worth checking if results seem disappointing.

The current UK injection instructions use gradual dose escalation, but Wegovy formulations and available doses are not interchangeable. Follow your own prescription and product leaflet. An older graphic showing a single 16–20-week route should not be used to choose a dose. Ask your prescriber what applies to the product you actually receive.

Clinical trials measure group outcomes over defined periods. The [STEP 3 trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33625476/) studied weekly semaglutide with intensive behavioural therapy; it does not establish a personal result or a date before which concerns should be ignored. Comparing your first few weeks with a trial's final average can create an unrealistic expectation.

Useful questions about the schedule include:

- What is my prescribed plan and next review date?
- What should I do if I cannot tolerate the current treatment?
- Who should advise me after an interruption or supply gap?
- Which symptoms mean I need urgent help?

A review can happen whenever there is a concern. Do not wait for maintenance or a fixed number of weeks to report symptoms or discuss a lack of progress.

## How side effects and tolerability can reduce effectiveness

Tolerability is part of whether treatment is suitable. A lower scale reading is not a good outcome if you cannot eat or drink adequately. Your prescriber may need to reconsider the plan; an article cannot determine the right change.

Digestive symptoms are recognised in the UK product information. Tell the service how severe they are, how long they last and what you can manage to eat and drink. This is more useful than describing every symptom as normal titration.

Do not push through severe symptoms to reach a higher dose. Nor should a coach or app advise you to change doses. Get appropriate clinical advice.

Not all symptoms are equal, though. [MHRA guidance for GLP-1 prescribers](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/mhra-updates-guidance-for-glp-1-prescribers-and-patients) flags severe abdominal pain as a red flag that needs urgent medical assessment, since it can indicate pancreatitis rather than routine gastrointestinal upset.

For mild symptoms, ask the prescribing team about practical food and fluid measures appropriate to you. If you cannot keep fluids down, symptoms persist or you feel unwell, seek medical advice rather than relying on self-care. Sudden vision loss also needs urgent assessment.

![Small balanced meal beside a glass of water](https://media.babylovegrowth.ai/blog-images/organization-55073/1790385228240_Small-balanced-meal-beside-a-glass-of-water.jpeg)

**Pro Tip:** *If nausea is putting you off food entirely rather than just reducing appetite, tell your prescriber. That's a sign to adjust the approach, not just tough it out.*

## Medical checks and investigations to consider if weight loss stalls

A clinician can consider whether a condition or another medicine is relevant to the change in weight. A plateau does not diagnose a thyroid problem, diabetes or an interaction. Bring new symptoms and medicine changes to the review rather than requesting the same panel of tests for everyone.

Some treatments and health conditions can affect weight, but do not stop a medicine prescribed for another condition. Ask the prescriber to review the whole list, including non-prescription products. If a test is suggested, ask what question it is intended to answer and how the result would change care.

A useful review checklist is:

- Review symptoms, medical history and the complete medicine list.
- Decide whether any tests are indicated for the individual circumstances.
- Remember that HbA1c assesses longer-term blood glucose; it is not a direct test for insulin resistance.
- Discuss whether specialist input would help and how a referral would work.

[NICE TA875](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ta875/chapter/1-recommendations) sets conditions for NHS use, including specialist-service provision. Those commissioning criteria should not be presented as the licensing conditions for every private prescription. Ask your own service which clinical and funding rules apply.

## Practical steps to improve response while staying safe

While waiting for a routine review, keep the plan manageable. These are options to discuss, not a promise that changing habits will overcome an inadequate medicine response:

1. **Keep meals workable:** record appetite and difficulties rather than automatically eating less.
2. **Choose suitable movement:** adapt activity to your ability and symptoms.
3. **Note sleep and stress:** mention persistent problems if they affect daily life.
4. **Describe alcohol and other products honestly:** include supplements and non-prescription medicines.
5. **Keep treatment records:** note prescribed doses, interruptions and questions for the pharmacist or prescriber.

The [NHS's calorie counting guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/better-health/lose-weight/calorie-counting/) is a solid, free starting point for structuring meals around a sensible deficit.

**Pro Tip:** *Pick one change from this list to focus on for a fortnight rather than trying to overhaul everything at once. Consistency beats intensity.*

Support should address practical barriers without blaming you for the outcome. Check which parts are clinical care and which are general coaching. Neither a programme nor a tracking tool can guarantee weight loss or replace an individual treatment decision.

## Clinical stopping rules, treatment duration and what happens if you stop or switch

Treatment needs review with your prescriber. The [current UK Wegovy product information](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/13800/smpc) says that, if weight loss is below 5% of starting weight after six months of treatment, the clinician needs to decide whether to continue after considering individual benefits and risks. This is six months on treatment, not six months after reaching a maintenance dose. NHS funding and service criteria are a separate question: check the current pathway with the service responsible for your care. Do not stop, increase or restart treatment using this article.

Stopping isn't necessarily the end of the story, though. Evidence from a withdrawal trial found that continuing semaglutide maintained further weight loss, while switching to placebo led to significant regain, with a statistically significant difference between groups over 48 weeks, according to [trial data on maintenance of weight loss](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33755728/). That's a strong signal that whatever weight loss you achieve on Wegovy tends to need an ongoing plan, whether that's continued medication, a structured maintenance approach, or both.

Key points to raise at a review:

- **Ask what your 6-month checkpoint result was** and what it means for continuing.
- **Agree a stopping or switching plan with your prescriber** if treatment is ending; this article does not provide a taper or restart schedule.
- **Plan for maintenance before you stop**, not after.

## Sources

- [Effect of Continued Once-Weekly Subcutaneous Semaglutide on Maintenance of Weight Loss in Adults With Overweight or Obesity](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33755728/)
- [Semaglutide for managing overweight and obesity (NICE TA875)](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ta875/chapter/1-recommendations)
- [Wegovy: EPAR — public assessment report (European Medicines Agency)](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/assessment-report/wegovy-epar-public-assessment-report_en.pdf)
- [MHRA updates guidance for GLP-1 prescribers and patients](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/mhra-updates-guidance-for-glp-1-prescribers-and-patients)

## FAQ

### Why am I not responding to Wegovy?

There are several possible explanations, including variation in response. Bring your treatment history, weight records and symptoms to a review. Do not assume that a slow result proves poor adherence or that a higher dose is the answer.

### How can I speed up weight loss on Wegovy?

Do not try to accelerate treatment by increasing doses, combining medicines or severely restricting food. Discuss whether the goal and plan remain appropriate. Safe care matters more than matching someone else's rate of loss.

### Why am I not losing anything on Wegovy?

A review can consider the exact medicine, treatment exposure, symptoms and relevant health factors. You do not need to wait until a particular week to ask for help, and no single online checklist can identify the cause.

### Why is Wegovy taking so long to work?

Titration and response vary, but a slow result should not be dismissed automatically. Ask your prescribing service when and how to assess benefit. The injection schedule and a trial's endpoint are different from your personal review needs.

## Recommended

- [Wegovy side effects and red flags](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/articles/wegovy-side-effects-timeline)
- [Wegovy vs orlistat](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/comparisons/medications/wegovy-vs-orlistat)
- [Wegovy injection and tablets](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/comparisons/medications/wegovy-injection-vs-tablets)
- [Wegovy vs Saxenda](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/comparisons/medications/wegovy-vs-saxenda)

## What My Timber can help with

Prepare your dose history, missed doses, symptoms and weight records for a review with your own prescriber. Do not increase, restart or switch medicine on the basis of an online article.

My Timber provides everyday support with food, movement, personal goals and progress records. It does not prescribe medicines, decide doses or provide a clinical review. Medicine assessment, prescribing, dispensing and treatment monitoring belong with your appropriately regulated healthcare provider.

SHIFT's medicine ordering remains closed while a prescribing partner is being commissioned. This page is information, not an invitation to buy prescription medicine or book a SHIFT prescribing assessment.

## Editorial correction — 2 October 2026

We removed unsupported descriptions of SHIFT clinical services and unapproved personal attribution where present. This correction does not represent an independent clinical review of the whole article.


Source correction — 3 October 2026: the review interval above is six months of treatment, not six months at maintenance. Checked against section 4.2 of the current UK Wegovy SmPC. This is an editorial source correction, not an independent clinical review.

## Source and editorial correction — 3 October 2026

This revision corrects unsupported timelines, universal rules and clinical claims, distinguishes study findings from personal expectations, and clarifies service boundaries. Original publication history is retained. This is an editorial source review, not independent clinical certification.

A clinician can consider whether a condition or another medicine is relevant to the change in weight. A plateau does not diagnose a thyroid problem, diabetes or an interaction. Bring new symptoms and medicine changes to the review rather than requesting the same panel of tests for everyone.

Some treatments and health conditions can affect weight, but do not stop a medicine prescribed for another condition. Ask the prescriber to review the whole list, including non-prescription products. If a test is suggested, ask what question it is intended to answer and how the result would change care.

A useful review checklist is:

- Review symptoms, medical history and the complete medicine list.
- Decide whether any tests are indicated for the individual circumstances.
- Remember that HbA1c assesses longer-term blood glucose; it is not a direct test for insulin resistance.
- Discuss whether specialist input would help and how a referral would work.

[NICE TA875](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ta875/chapter/1-recommendations) sets conditions for NHS use, including specialist-service provision. Those commissioning criteria should not be presented as the licensing conditions for every private prescription. Ask your own service which clinical and funding rules apply.

While waiting for a routine review, keep the plan manageable. These are options to discuss, not a promise that changing habits will overcome an inadequate medicine response:

1. **Keep meals workable:** record appetite and difficulties rather than automatically eating less.
2. **Choose suitable movement:** adapt activity to your ability and symptoms.
3. **Note sleep and stress:** mention persistent problems if they affect daily life.
4. **Describe alcohol and other products honestly:** include supplements and non-prescription medicines.
5. **Keep treatment records:** note prescribed doses, interruptions and questions for the pharmacist or prescriber.

Treatment needs review with your prescriber. This is six months on treatment, not six months after reaching a maintenance dose. NHS funding and service criteria are a separate question: check the current pathway with the service responsible for your care. Do not stop, increase or restart treatment using this article.

Stopping isn't necessarily the end of the story, though. That's a strong signal that whatever weight loss you achieve on Wegovy tends to need an ongoing plan, whether that's continued medication, a structured maintenance approach, or both.

Key points to raise at a review:

- **Ask what your 6-month checkpoint result was** and what it means for continuing.
- **Agree a stopping or switching plan with your prescriber** if treatment is ending; this article does not provide a taper or restart schedule.
- **Plan for maintenance before you stop**, not after.

- [Effect of Continued Once-Weekly Subcutaneous Semaglutide on Maintenance of Weight Loss in Adults With Overweight or Obesity](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33755728/)
- [Semaglutide for managing overweight and obesity (NICE TA875)](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ta875/chapter/1-recommendations)
- [Wegovy: EPAR — public assessment report (European Medicines Agency)](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/assessment-report/wegovy-epar-public-assessment-report_en.pdf)
- [MHRA updates guidance for GLP-1 prescribers and patients](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/mhra-updates-guidance-for-glp-1-prescribers-and-patients)

## FAQ

### Why am I not responding to Wegovy?

There are several possible explanations, including variation in response. Bring your treatment history, weight records and symptoms to a review. Do not assume that a slow result proves poor adherence or that a higher dose is the answer.

### How can I speed up weight loss on Wegovy?

Do not try to accelerate treatment by increasing doses, combining medicines or severely restricting food. Discuss whether the goal and plan remain appropriate. Safe care matters more than matching someone else's rate of loss.

### Why am I not losing anything on Wegovy?

A review can consider the exact medicine, treatment exposure, symptoms and relevant health factors. You do not need to wait until a particular week to ask for help, and no single online checklist can identify the cause.

### Why is Wegovy taking so long to work?

Titration and response vary, but a slow result should not be dismissed automatically. Ask your prescribing service when and how to assess benefit. The injection schedule and a trial's endpoint are different from your personal review needs.

## Recommended

- [Wegovy side effects and red flags](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/articles/wegovy-side-effects-timeline)
- [Wegovy vs orlistat](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/comparisons/medications/wegovy-vs-orlistat)
- [Wegovy injection and tablets](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/comparisons/medications/wegovy-injection-vs-tablets)
- [Wegovy vs Saxenda](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/comparisons/medications/wegovy-vs-saxenda)

Prepare your dose history, missed doses, symptoms and weight records for a review with your own prescriber. Do not increase, restart or switch medicine on the basis of an online article.

[My Timber](/my-timber) provides everyday support with food, movement, personal goals and progress records. It does not prescribe medicines, decide doses or provide a clinical review. Medicine assessment, prescribing, dispensing and treatment monitoring belong with your appropriately regulated healthcare provider.

before.summary: Binge eating needs appropriate assessment and support. Understand the limits of medicine claims and prepare questions for an eating-disorder care conversation.
before.body:
# Binge eating and weight-loss medicines: keep the treatment questions separate

Repeated episodes of eating with a sense of losing control deserve appropriate support. They are not something you have to solve by being stricter, and a weight-loss medicine is not automatically a treatment for an eating disorder.

## Start with an assessment, not a medicine recommendation

Tell a GP or appropriate healthcare professional what happens, how often, how you feel afterwards and how it affects your life. You do not need to prove that your weight is high enough or that the episodes are severe enough to ask for help.

Eating-disorder care needs to consider the whole situation, including mental and physical health. A diagnosis cannot be made from a calorie log, an online quiz or a coaching conversation. If you have already been prescribed a medicine for another purpose, tell the clinician assessing your eating difficulties about it.

## What established guidance says

NICE recommends eating-disorder-focused support for binge eating disorder, starting with guided self-help where appropriate and considering further psychological treatment according to the person's needs. It advises against medication as the sole treatment for binge eating disorder.

The NHS explains that trying to diet during treatment can make it harder to stop binge eating. Discuss food changes and any weight-management treatment with the team looking after you rather than combining conflicting plans yourself.

## Research is not an individual treatment recommendation

Interest in how GLP-1 medicines affect appetite does not establish that any particular medicine is an approved or suitable treatment for your eating disorder. A small or early study is not equivalent to a large controlled trial, a licence or an individual assessment. This article does not recommend starting, stopping or changing a medicine to manage binge eating.

If you are considering a study or a proposed off-label treatment, ask the clinician what evidence supports it, what uncertainty remains, how safety is monitored and what established options are available. Do not buy a medicine without a legitimate prescription or use a product sold as a research peptide.

## Prepare for the conversation

- Describe the episodes in your own words, including the sense of control and the distress involved.
- Mention restriction, fasting, vomiting, laxative use or excessive exercise if these occur.
- Bring your medicine list and tell the clinician about other health conditions.
- Ask how to obtain eating-disorder support locally and what to do while waiting.
- Say if tracking food, weight or calories makes the difficulty worse.

These notes are preparation for care, not a checklist you must complete before receiving help. Seek urgent medical help for an immediate safety concern rather than waiting to build a diary.

## Where SHIFT fits

My Timber can organise everyday goals if that is useful to you. It is not an eating-disorder treatment, symptom assessment or monitored clinical service. You can pause tracking that is unhelpful and seek appropriate care independently of a SHIFT purchase. SHIFT medicine ordering remains closed while the regulated partner is not commissioned.

## Sources and editorial note

- [NICE NG69: recognising and treating eating disorders](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng69/chapter/recommendations).
- [NHS: treatment for binge eating disorder](https://www.nhs.uk/mental-health/conditions/binge-eating/treatment/).
- [NHS: binge eating disorder](https://www.nhs.uk/mental-health/conditions/binge-eating/).

Editorial correction: 2 October 2026. Medicine promotion and unsupported treatment implications have been removed. General information; independent clinical review is not claimed.

before.body:
# Semaglutide results: timelines and review points

![Decorative semaglutide timeline title card](https://media.babylovegrowth.ai/blog-images/organization-55073/1790548883051_Decorative-semaglutide-timeline-title-card.jpeg)

There is no week when everyone should first feel or see semaglutide working. Appetite, weight and side effects vary, and a study's end date is not a personal deadline. This guide explains the 68-week STEP 1 result, how to keep useful records and when to raise concerns. The injection study discussed here should not be treated as evidence for an identical tablet timeline.

***

> **Key points**
>
> - Trial averages cannot predict a particular person's weekly results.
> - Dose schedules depend on the product and your prescribed plan.
> - A 68-week research endpoint is not a reason to delay a review.
> - Symptoms may need urgent attention at any stage.
> - Record your experience and discuss concerns with your own prescriber.

***

## Why a week-by-week promise is misleading

Some people notice changes in appetite before a sustained change on the scales, while others have a different experience. Neither a strong appetite effect nor nausea proves that treatment is effective or safe. Conversely, not feeling an immediate change does not establish treatment failure. Use your agreed review plan and raise concerns rather than comparing yourself with a fixed internet timetable.

The [STEP 1 study](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03548935) used a gradual escalation to once-weekly injected semaglutide 2.4 mg. Trial participants followed a defined protocol. In practice, symptoms, interruptions and individual decisions can affect treatment. Even two people on the same dose can respond differently, so a friend's week-by-week account is not a reliable benchmark.

A more useful way to organise the treatment period is:

1. **Before starting:** understand the exact product, prescription instructions, contact arrangements and review plan.
2. **During dose changes:** record the prescribed dose and any symptoms; ask for advice before making changes yourself.
3. **At planned reviews:** assess benefits, tolerability and whether the plan remains appropriate.
4. **Between reviews:** contact the service about concerns, especially poor intake, persistent symptoms or lack of progress.
5. **When reading research:** check the study population, product, dose and endpoint before comparing its results with your own.

Weight can fluctuate and a slower period does not by itself establish why progress has changed. A trend over time is more informative than a single reading. Do not automatically cut food further or increase medicine in response to a plateau; review the situation with your care team.

## Why your semaglutide weight loss progress may differ from average trial figures

Trial averages describe a group, not a person, and several factors pull individual timelines away from that average.

- **Product and dose:** an injection trial does not establish an identical result for tablets or another medicine.
- **Study population:** age, diabetes status and other eligibility criteria affect how relevant a trial is to you.
- **Treatment exposure:** interruptions, tolerability and time on treatment matter, but do not let anyone assume slow progress is your fault.
- **Other health factors:** tell your prescriber about new diagnoses, symptoms or medicines.
- **Outcome measurement:** a group average does not show the whole spread of individual responses.

**Pro Tip:** *Track your progress against your own baseline, not against someone else's photos or a trial average: your starting weight, dose and diabetic status all mean your timeline is genuinely your own.*

## What the UK clinical pathway means for your titration schedule

Semaglutide is prescription-only in the UK, and that single fact shapes almost everything about how the timeline actually runs in practice. It isn't something you start and adjust on your own; it comes with a clinical assessment, a structured titration schedule and scheduled check-ins.

1. **Assessment:** a prescriber considers suitability and explains the specific product.
2. **Prescription instructions:** follow the agreed schedule and ask about symptoms or interruptions before changing it.
3. **Review timing:** confirm when the service will review you and how to get earlier help.
4. **Continuation decisions:** assess benefits and risks individually, alongside any separate NHS funding criteria.

Practical questions include storage, administration, missed doses and contact arrangements. For injections, ask about sharps disposal. Tell the anaesthetic team about treatment before surgery or deep sedation. Pregnancy and contraception advice should be medicine-specific where relevant. NHS access routes also vary between UK nations; a regional Scottish protocol is not a UK-wide prescribing rule.

## What STEP 1 actually measured

STEP 1 studied adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes. Both groups received lifestyle support; one group received injected semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly and the other placebo. Its results describe that study population and treatment, not SHIFT patients or a men-only trial.

The [STEP 1 report](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2032183) reported average weight changes at 68 weeks of −14.9% with semaglutide and −2.4% with placebo. Individuals varied. These figures do not promise that you will lose the average amount, reach it by a particular month or follow a straight line towards it.

A trial endpoint is chosen so researchers can compare groups. It is not a definition of when a medicine has 'fully worked', and it does not set the date of your first clinical review. Ask which outcomes matter for your own care and how they will be assessed. Weight, tolerability and relevant health measures may all enter that discussion.

## Side effects and safety checks that shape your timeline

Digestive symptoms can occur during treatment and dose escalation, but there is no guaranteed settling period. Tell your prescriber if symptoms persist, worsen or interfere with eating and drinking. Severe symptoms need assessment rather than reassurance that they are simply part of a timetable.

- **Severe, persistent abdominal pain:** seek urgent medical attention; pain may extend to the back and occur with vomiting.
- **Sudden loss or rapid worsening of vision:** seek urgent assessment.
- **Ongoing vomiting or difficulty keeping fluids down:** get prompt medical advice.
- **Milder troublesome symptoms:** contact your prescribing service for advice before the next planned change.

The [UK Wegovy product information](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/13800/smpc) describes safety precautions and individual continuation decisions. It calls for a benefits-and-risks decision when adult weight loss is below 5% after six months of treatment. That interval starts with treatment, not after reaching maintenance. It does not mean waiting six months to report symptoms.

## How to track progress and respond if results are slower than expected

A short record can make a review more useful. Note the date, prescribed dose, weight if you are tracking it, symptoms and whether you can eat and drink normally. Include questions you want answered. Measurements taken under similar conditions are easier to compare, but you do not need constant weighing to justify asking for help.

1. **Use consistent records:** avoid comparing different scales or isolated readings as if they were precise trends.
2. **Record tolerability:** note when symptoms began and what they prevent you doing.
3. **Contact the right service:** urgent symptoms need urgent care; routine concerns can go to your prescriber.
4. **Agree the next review:** ask what information the clinician needs and what should trigger earlier contact.

**Pro Tip:** *Pair the medication with consistent behavioural support: the trial evidence behind semaglutide was generated alongside diet and activity counselling, not the drug on its own.*

## Sources

- [MHRA: GLP-1 medicine information](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/glp-1-medicines-for-weight-loss-and-diabetes-what-you-need-to-know)
- [STEP 1 primary report](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2032183)
- [STEP 1 trial registration](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03548935)
- [UK Wegovy injection product information](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/13800/smpc)

## FAQ

### How much weight will I lose in 2 months on semaglutide?

There is no reliable personal two-month prediction. Early treatment may still involve dose changes, depending on the product and plan. Record your experience and ask your prescriber about concerns; the 68-week trial average cannot be converted into an expected monthly loss.

### How quickly do you lose weight on semaglutide?

There is no universal onset or rate. Appetite and weight can change differently between people. An exact four-to-twelve-week promise is not established by the study result discussed here.

### How many weeks to see results from semaglutide?

STEP 1 assessed its main outcome at 68 weeks, but that is a research endpoint, not a deadline for seeing a result. Your care team should set appropriate reviews and explain when to contact them sooner.

### I am 8 weeks on semaglutide and I haven't lost any weight. Is this normal?

Raise the concern with your prescriber. They can review the product, actual treatment history, symptoms and relevant health factors. Do not increase the dose or restrict food aggressively to catch up with an online timeline.

## Recommended

- [Oral semaglutide: interpreting the evidence](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/articles/oral-semaglutide-for-weight-loss)
- [Lean mass and GLP-1 treatment](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/articles/glp-1-muscle-loss)
- [Stopping GLP-1 treatment](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/articles/stopping-glp1)
- [Muscle and everyday strength](https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/articles/muscle-on-glp1)

## What My Timber can help with

Record your actual experience instead of comparing each week with a promised timeline. Ask your own prescriber what they expect from your particular medicine, dose and circumstances.

My Timber provides everyday support with food, movement, personal goals and progress records. It does not prescribe medicines, decide doses or provide a clinical review. Medicine assessment, prescribing, dispensing and treatment monitoring belong with your appropriately regulated healthcare provider.

SHIFT's medicine ordering remains closed while a prescribing partner is being commissioned. This page is information, not an invitation to buy prescription medicine or book a SHIFT prescribing assessment.

## Editorial correction — 2 October 2026

We removed unsupported descriptions of SHIFT clinical services and unapproved personal attribution where present. This correction does not represent an independent clinical review of the whole article.

## Source and editorial correction — 3 October 2026

This revision corrects unsupported timelines, universal rules and clinical claims, distinguishes study findings from personal expectations, and clarifies service boundaries. Original publication history is retained. This is an editorial source review, not independent clinical certification.

# GLP-1 medicines for men: questions for your prescriber

![Decorative GLP-1 muscle loss title card](https://media.babylovegrowth.ai/blog-images/organization-55073/1790641307057_Decorative-GLP-1-muscle-loss-title-card.jpeg)

GLP-1 medicines may be considered for weight management after an individual assessment. For men, useful questions include treatment goals, side effects, strength, sexual health and other medicines. Research on reproductive markers does not establish GLP-1 treatment as a fertility therapy or a substitute for testosterone treatment. This guide helps you prepare a clinical discussion rather than decide suitability yourself.

***

> **Key points**
>
> - Suitability and follow-up depend on the specific product and individual circumstances.
> - Reproductive research is not a promise of improved fertility or testosterone.
> - New symptoms, including sexual-health changes, deserve a clinical discussion.
> - Ask about food intake and strength if weight loss affects daily function.
> - Tell your care teams about all medicines and any planned procedure.

***

## How GLP-1 medicines work in the body

GLP-1 receptor agonists act on signalling involved in appetite and blood-glucose regulation. Tirzepatide acts on both GIP and GLP-1 receptors. The effects and practical instructions depend on the medicine; this brief description is not the whole mechanism or an explanation of every symptom a person might notice.

Products differ in formulation, dose, indication and administration. An oral tablet and an injection are not interchangeable on a milligram-for-milligram basis. Check the exact name and leaflet, and ask a pharmacist if instructions are unclear. Do not apply another person's injection or tablet schedule to your prescription.

Many products use dose escalation to help tolerability, but the schedule is product-specific. Increasing more slowly does not guarantee freedom from side effects, and symptoms can arise outside dose changes. Follow the prescription and ask for advice rather than designing your own escalation.

## Benefits for men: weight loss and reproductive health signals

Weight loss on GLP-1 medicines varies from person to person, and it's best treated as a realistic range rather than a promise, since trial results differ by drug, dose and how long someone stays on treatment.

A [systematic review of reproductive outcomes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41498523/) examines hormones, semen measures and metabolic outcomes. Such measures are not equivalent to pregnancy or live-birth outcomes, and a review does not establish treatment for infertility. If you have symptoms of testosterone deficiency or fertility concerns, seek the appropriate assessment rather than choosing a weight-management medicine for an unproven reproductive benefit.

The reproductive picture isn't entirely one-directional. Some observational data have linked semaglutide use to a higher rate of new erectile dysfunction diagnoses, which we'll come back to shortly. Nothing here proves cause and effect, but it's worth raising with your clinician rather than assuming it doesn't apply to you.

## Side effects and safety: what to expect and what to escalate

Nausea, vomiting, constipation and diarrhoea can occur. Tell the prescriber if symptoms persist or interfere with eating and drinking. General food measures may help mild symptoms, but they do not replace assessment or justify changing a dose yourself.

A smaller number of men experience something more serious. The [MHRA has strengthened its warnings on acute pancreatitis](https://www.gov.uk/drug-safety-update/glp-1-receptor-agonists-and-dual-glp-1-slash-gip-receptor-agonists-strengthened-warnings-on-acute-pancreatitis-including-necrotising-and-fatal-cases) linked to GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP medicines, including rare but necrotising and fatal cases. Know the red flags:

Seek urgent medical attention for severe, persistent abdominal pain, particularly if it reaches the back or occurs with vomiting. Do not wait to see whether paracetamol or a different position makes it manageable.

**Practical safety point:** Know the urgent-care route before treatment starts. A coach, progress tracker or routine message inbox is not the right route for an emergency.

The [TriNetX database study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38778151/) compared matched men aged 18–50 with obesity and without diabetes. It found more recorded erectile-dysfunction diagnoses or related prescriptions in the semaglutide group. This observational association cannot show that semaglutide caused the difference, and it should not be generalised to every man. Discuss a new sexual-health problem rather than diagnosing a drug effect yourself.

Weight change can involve fat and lean tissue. Lean mass is not identical to skeletal muscle or strength, and the proportions vary. Discuss adequate intake, suitable activity and any new functional difficulty with your care team. Exercise and protein do not guarantee that all lean-tissue loss can be prevented.

![Man performing resistance training with dumbbells](https://media.babylovegrowth.ai/blog-images/organization-55073/1790641367418_Man-performing-resistance-training-with-dumbbells.jpeg)

## Who can get GLP-1 treatment and how access works

Medicine licensing, NHS funding criteria and immediate local availability are different questions. [NICE's medicine guidance](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng246/chapter/Medicines-and-surgery) distinguishes products; there is no single BMI rule that applies to every GLP-1 medicine and prescribing route.

- Ask which specific medicine and indication are being considered.
- Check the relevant NHS pathway and UK nation if seeking NHS care.
- Ask how any ethnicity-adjusted threshold applies to that pathway.
- Confirm the clinical assessment, follow-up and support arrangements whether care is NHS or private.

GLP-1 medicines are prescription only, whichever route you take. NHS availability depends on local commissioning and specialist referral pathways, which is why access varies so much by area and why many men who meet the criteria still end up looking at private options. Whichever route you choose, the medicine should sit inside proper clinical oversight rather than being self-sourced.

## Starting treatment: titration, monitoring and protecting your muscle

Ask for written instructions for the exact medicine and a clear review plan. A schedule that is appropriate for one product may be wrong for another. Before starting, make sure you can answer these practical questions:

1. What dose and administration instructions have I been prescribed?
2. Whom do I contact about symptoms before the next dose or change?
3. What should I do after a missed dose or a supply interruption?
4. Which checks are indicated for my health, and when is the next review?
5. How can I get help if appetite loss makes adequate eating difficult?

**Pro tip:** *Track your strength, not just the scales, since a falling number on the scale tells you nothing about whether you're losing fat or muscle.*

A change in body weight does not show how much is fat or lean tissue. Discuss concerns about strength or body composition with your clinician.

## Surgery and anaesthesia: why you must disclose GLP-1 use

GLP-1 medicines slow gastric emptying, and that can raise the risk of pulmonary aspiration during general anaesthesia or deep sedation, even after a standard fast. Anaesthetists won't necessarily know about a private prescription unless you tell them, so carry your prescription details to any pre-op assessment.

Expect an individual risk assessment. Your anaesthetic team may adjust fasting instructions, timing, or the choice of sedation based on your treatment history, so raise it early rather than on the day of surgery.

## Stopping treatment: what happens to your appetite and weight

Appetite and weight often creep back once treatment stops, since the hormonal effect that suppressed "food noise" fades along with the drug. That's a physiological pattern, not a personal failure.

Plan follow-up with your prescriber when treatment is ending. Practical support may help with routines, but cannot guarantee that weight regain will be avoided or slowed. Do not use a general article as a tapering or restarting schedule. Ask what to monitor, when to review and which options may be considered if concerns arise.

## Interactions with blood pressure, cholesterol and testosterone medicines

Bring a complete list of prescribed medicines, over-the-counter products and supplements. Blood pressure or glucose treatment may need review as health changes, but do not adjust it yourself. Tell the clinician about dizziness, faintness or other new symptoms so they can assess the cause rather than assuming a dose has become too high.

Potential interactions and administration requirements depend on the exact products. Ask a pharmacist to check the complete list, particularly when a new medicine is added. Do not move all tablets around meals simply because GLP-1 medicines can affect stomach emptying. Follow each medicine's own instructions.

If you use testosterone, tell both prescribing teams. Emerging reproductive research does not by itself justify increasing, reducing or stopping testosterone. Assessment of symptoms and any indicated tests belongs with the treating clinician. Carry your medicine list to appointments rather than assuming separate services automatically share every update.

## Mood and mental health while on GLP-1 treatment

Experiences of appetite and mood vary. Some people describe less preoccupation with food; others find changes in eating difficult. This article cannot establish how common either experience is or promise a mental-health benefit.

Tell your clinician about persistent low mood, anxiety, distress about eating or changes that affect daily life. Do not dismiss these simply because weight is falling. A lifestyle coach can listen and help you find the right service, but should not diagnose or treat a mental-health condition outside their competence.

Discuss a history of disordered eating or mental-health difficulties during assessment so care can reflect it. Whether a medicine is appropriate needs individual judgment; this history is neither an automatic approval nor an automatic exclusion that an article can determine.

## Long-term safety: what to keep an eye on over time

Evidence and safety information develop over time, and the amount of follow-up differs between products and indications. Ask the prescriber about the known benefits, risks and uncertainties relevant to the proposed treatment. Keep using the current product leaflet and clinical advice rather than treating an old article as permanent guidance.

Monitoring should be individualised. Ask which measures are useful for you and why, rather than assuming everyone needs repeated body-composition scans or the same blood tests. Persistent symptoms, inadequate intake or declining strength should be discussed between scheduled reviews when needed.

If supply is interrupted, contact the prescribing service or pharmacy. Do not substitute another product or resume a previous high dose without advice. Historic shortage notices describe the situation at their publication date; they do not establish today's stock position.

## Questions worth asking your prescriber before you start

A good clinical conversation covers more than eligibility. Before you commit, it's worth asking your prescriber:

- Which specific medicine and dose are you recommending, and why that one for me.
- What does the titration schedule look like, and how will side effects be reviewed.
- How will you monitor for muscle loss, and what's the plan if it happens.
- What happens if I develop severe abdominal pain or notice sexual side effects.
- How will you manage a supply shortage or a planned surgery while I'm on treatment.

A prescriber who welcomes these questions and answers them clearly is a good sign that you're in a properly governed pathway rather than a one-off medication sale.

## Fitting GLP-1 treatment around alcohol and smoking

Tell your prescriber about alcohol intake, especially if it affects eating, hydration or other medicines. This article does not establish a predictable change in alcohol absorption on treatment. Ask about individual risks rather than assuming either that alcohol is harmless or that a particular drink limit makes it safe for everyone.

Smoking is relevant to general health and deserves its own support if you want to stop. It should be discussed honestly during assessment alongside other health factors, without presenting weight-management treatment as a substitute for smoking-cessation care.

Neither habit needs to be perfect before you start treatment, but be honest with your prescriber about both. It affects how they interpret side effects, monitor your progress and judge whether your dose or pace needs adjusting.

## Sources

- [NICE guidance: a guide for prescribing medicines to manage overweight and obesity — medicine options for weight management in adults](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng246/resources/a-guide-for-prescribing-medicines-to-manage-overweight-and-obesity-15299628589/chapter/Medicine-options-for-weight-management-in-adults)
- [MHRA drug safety update: GLP‑1 receptor agonists and dual GLP‑1/GIP receptor agonists — strengthened warnings on acute pancreatitis](https://www.gov.uk/drug-safety-update/glp-1-receptor-agonists-and-dual-glp-1-slash-gip-receptor-agonists-strengthened-warnings-on-acute-pancreatitis-including-necrotising-and-fatal-cases)
- [Effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on male reproductive hormones, semen parameters, and metabolic outcomes: a systematic review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41498523/)
